behavioral_effects: SessionStart injects a bounded orientation map (~1.2k tokens) with a gate health line
Bulk enumeration of governance/history and governance/manifests warns with query-instead instructions; named-file reads always pass
Stop blocks turn-end with exact repair commands while touched files lack a change session or record
sync now emits read-surface.json compiled from component ownership, the catalog, sanctioned locations, and the governance.toml [gate] table
compatibility_impact: governance summary is now read-only where it previously ran a full sync under a read-only-sounding name; scripts and hook JSON are additive; read-surface.json is a new generated manifest validated by a kernel-internal schema
follow_up: Phase 3: owner-observed live checklist including the degraded drill
Phase 4: coverage verifier, CI gate smoke step, per-surface deny decisions
Phase 5: chat-retention and token-accounting regression tests
limitations: Hooks take effect only after session restart: the Phase 3 live acceptance checklist is pending owner observation
Both gate surfaces stay in warn until the Phase 4 coverage measurement justifies deny per surface
PreToolUse warn notes surface via user-visible systemMessage, not model context - Claude Code offers no context injection on an allow decision
reason: The governance system is advisory - nothing makes an agent consult it, keep it fresh, or stay inside it; observed failures include 300k-token unguided exploration and changes shipped without records. Wires the existing CLI into Claude Code lifecycle hooks per the approved v2 plan: compact map at session start, corpus bulk-reads gated via a sync-generated artifact read by stdlib scripts, turn-end blocked until records and freshness hold
rollback: git revert restores code, config, and manifests; hook state under .cache/repo-governance/hooks/ is unversioned scratch and can be deleted; hooks deactivate on the next session start after revert
security_impact: Hooks execute repo-committed scripts only; the read gate is fail-open steering (deny requires positive certainty), never a security boundary; session state lives under gitignored .cache; GOVERNANCE_GATE escape hatch is environment-set by the user, outside agent reach; no network, credentials, or secret paths touched
summary: Hook-enforced governance: read-surface artifact, gate scripts, session and stop hooks
